subject: Token count discrepancy & proposed customer credit
messages:
From: Alex Hsu <alex.hsu@acme-corp.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: billing@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected duplicate charges on Feb invoice — token counts look doubled

Hi Marissa / Markus,

We noticed our February invoice shows unusually high token usage for a handful of routes after the 2026-02-28 maintenance window. The per-route usage spikes suggest some requests were counted twice. Attached is the invoice extract for the routes in question. Can you confirm whether this is an error on our side or something on the Redwood side?

We need to reconcile before our procurement team issues payment — this increase would materially change our Q1 spend.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Hsu
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
alex.hsu@acme-corp.com

Hi Alex — thanks for flagging this and for sending the invoice extract. We’re sorry for the surprise; I’ve opened a ticket with our billing and SRE teams and looped in Priyom for an initial investigation.

Can you confirm the approximate time window of requests (you included the invoice snippet, but any timestamps or request IDs on your side would help us correlate) and whether you saw any 5xx errors at the same time? We’ll prioritize this.

I’ll keep you posted with findings and next steps by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:42:36 -0700
Subject: RE: Unexpected duplicate charges on Feb invoice — token counts look doubled

Marissa / Markus,

Quick internal summary from SRE/billing investigation:
- Incident ID: RW-2026-03-TOK-01 (started 2026-02-28 22:13:07 UTC)
- Root cause: a short-lived failover path in our request routing code failed to clear in-flight token accounting when connections were retried, causing a subset of requests to be double-counted by the billing pipeline for ~4m between 22:13:07–22:17:30 UTC.
- Impact: approximately 0.7% of total platform tokens during that window were duplicated (we correlate to the route IDs in Acme’s invoice extract).
- Mitigation applied: fix deployed to routing path at 22:26 UTC, and billing pipeline dedup job run on 2026-03-02 03:10 UTC to attempt automatic correction.

We attached the debug logs and the dedup job run summary for your reference. Our initial estimate is that Acme’s invoice was overstated by $3,420 (USD) for the period in question. We recommend applying a credit for the next invoice and also offering a one-time goodwill credit of $500 to acknowledge the inconvenience.

Attachments included: redwood-debug-log-20260302.txt (excerpt), dedup-run-20260302-summary.csv (small).

Let me know if you want more granular per-request data — we can redact any customer PII before sharing.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
SRE, Billing & Payments | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

----
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hsu <alex.hsu@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 15:10:08 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate charges on Feb invoice — token counts look doubled

Hi Alex —

First, thank you for bringing this to our attention and apologies for the disruption. I want to be transparent about what happened and our proposed remediation:

What happened (short summary):
- During a maintenance-driven failover at 2026-02-28 22:13 UTC, a routing retry path did not clear token accounting correctly. A small fraction of requests were double-counted for ~4 minutes.
- The SRE team detected the anomaly, deployed a fix, and ran a billing deduplication job; however, the dedup job did not fully reconcile all customer invoices.

What we are doing for Acme:
- Credit: We will apply a corrective credit of $3,420 against your March invoice to fully offset the duplicate charges.
- Goodwill: We'll add a one-time $500 goodwill credit on top of that for the inconvenience.
- Postmortem: Full incident postmortem is published here: https://redwood.app/postmortems/RW-2026-03-token-count (summary attached).
- Next steps: longer-term fix already in our deployment queue to improve idempotency at the billing ingress and additional end-to-end billing verification tests before releases.

Proposed timeline: Apply the corrective credit against your March invoice (to be reflected 2026-03-10). If you prefer an immediate refund instead of an invoice credit, we can arrange that with your accounting contact — please let us know.

Would you like me to proceed with applying the invoice credit as outlined, or should we arrange a refund to your payment method?

Apologies again, and thank you for your patience while we sorted this out.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0148

Hi Markus / Marissa —

Thanks for the clear explanation and for the quick turnaround. Applying the $3,420 corrective credit plus the $500 goodwill credit to our March invoice is fine — please proceed with the invoice credit.

For our records, could you confirm the credit will appear on the March invoice and that we do not need to submit any forms on our side? Our billing team (billing@acme-corp.com) is copied — they prefer credits to appear on the next invoice rather than separate refunds.

Appreciate the postmortem link and the follow-up.

Best,
Alex
